reason: CLI awaited stdout drain without sharing the export deadline. An open nonreading pipe retained a pending OS write and kept the executable alive after the download deadline.

regression.test: executable export deadline terminates with a real open nonreading stdout pipe
regression.before: Failed: actual stdout.write returned false; original CLI remained alive until the 1500ms watchdog killed it.
regression.after: Passed: real write delegates to OS pipe; abort armed only after backpressure marker. CLI exits 2 without watchdog in both stdout-only and stdout-plus-stderr blocked cases.
regression.testHarnessLimitation: Transport generator supplies a large provisional fixture to isolate actual CLI pipe behavior; domain/export verification is covered by separate transport and real-service tests.

diagnosis: Sharing signal with drain resolved the asynchronous wait, but stdout.destroy alone did not terminate the process.
Adding stdout.unref also failed to terminate a retained pending OS write; that experiment was removed.

fix.behavior: CLI-owned120s signal shared by modelReviewExport and stdout drain. On deadline, discard pending stdout and force CLI exit2 after redacted stderr callback or100ms fallback. Public client never exits caller process.
